title: How to choose the best Update Window in Dynamics 365 Business Central Online
summary: Explains how to pick a Business Central Online update window so that application hotfixes, which follow the 6-hour window set in Tenant Admin Center, and most platform hotfixes, which Microsoft times itself, fall in the same period. Gives KQL telemetry queries that count platform hotfix deployments by local hour and weekday to guide job queue scheduling.
key_points: Application hotfixes follow the per-environment 6-hour update window and can be tracked with telemetry signal LC0159; platform hotfixes roll out node by node at times Microsoft decides
Background sessions and web services get no UI warning, so long jobs such as MRP can break and log errors in Job Queue Log Entry
The KQL query removes version changes caused by planned upgrades, converts UTC to local time and groups platform hotfix changes by hour or weekday
For Italian environments the best 6-hour window was 2 to 8 AM, and platform hotfixes were rare before midnight
Tuesday and Friday showed fewer platform hotfixes, Wednesday and Thursday the most, and weekends almost none

quotes.text: Application Hotfixes typically observe the 6-hours Update Window setup per environment in Tenant Admin Center.
quotes.why_it_matters: Shows that application hotfixes are controllable, unlike platform hotfixes which deploy independently

quotes.text: These are critical components and/or platform changes that are applied node by node in the cluster that is serving multiple customers.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains why platform hotfixes cannot follow the update window schedule and impact multiple environments

quotes.text: If you want to plan the best update window for your customer, you must use telemetry to better understand when platform hotfixes are applied.
quotes.why_it_matters: Provides the key strategy for minimizing disruptions by using data-driven analysis rather than assumptions
